content.tip: values đếm được, số nhiều → are.

content.why: **a number of** + danh từ số nhiều → động từ số nhiều: **are**.

content.q: The amount of data ___ every year.
content.tip: the amount of + N không đếm được → V số ít.
content.why: **the amount of data** → động từ số ít: **grows**.

content.q: How ___ rows does the table have?

exercises.title: Bài 1 · What does a data scientist do?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Every day, companies collect a huge amount of data: sales records, website visits, photos and customer emails. Data science is the field that turns this data into useful knowledge. A data scientist does not only write code. She also needs statistics and domain knowledge, so that she understands the business problem.

The workflow usually starts with a question, for example: "Why are customers leaving?" First, the team collects the data. A data engineer builds the pipelines that move and store it. After that, a data analyst or data scientist explores the data to find patterns and trends. Next, the scientist may build a model to predict which customers will leave. Finally, the team shares the insights with stakeholders, often in a dashboard.

Good projects are data-driven and reproducible: another person can run the same notebook and get the same results. This is why data scientists write clear code and keep notes about every step.

content.q: A data scientist only writes code.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cô ấy còn cần **statistics** và **domain knowledge**.

content.q: A data engineer builds the pipelines that move and store data.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'A data engineer builds the pipelines…'.

content.q: The team explores the data after it presents the insights.
content.why: Đoạn 2: khám phá dữ liệu diễn ra **trước**, chia sẻ insight là bước **cuối**.

content.q: A reproducible project gives the same results when another person runs the notebook.
content.why: Đoạn 3: người khác chạy cùng notebook và nhận cùng kết quả.

content.q: What does the workflow usually start with?
content.why: Đoạn 2: quy trình thường bắt đầu bằng **một câu hỏi**.

content.q: Who explores the data to find patterns and trends?
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'a data analyst or data scientist explores the data'.
opts: A data analyst or a data scientist

content.q: Why does a data scientist need domain knowledge?
content.why: Đoạn 1: 'so that she understands the business problem'.

content.q: Why do data scientists keep notes about every step?
content.why: Đoạn 3: để dự án có thể tái lập (reproducible).
opts: So that their work is reproducible

exercises.passage:
Hi Linh,
Welcome to the analytics team! This week you are going to learn how we work. On Monday you will meet the stakeholders from marketing. They are worried because sales growth has slowed down. Our main KPI is the monthly repeat-purchase rate, and it fell from 32% to 27% in two quarters.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, you will explore the dataset in a notebook. Please check how many observations have missing values, and note any unusual pattern. You must not change the raw data: always work on a copy.

On Thursday you will present your first insights. A short slide deck is enough, but include one clear chart. Do not hesitate to ask me if you need domain knowledge about our products.
Best wishes,
Hoa, Head of Analytics

content.why: Đoạn 1: 'On Monday you will meet the stakeholders from marketing'.

content.q: The main KPI is the monthly repeat-purchase rate.

content.why: Đoạn 3: cô ấy trình bày vào **Thursday**.

content.why: Đoạn 1: tăng trưởng doanh số đã chậm lại.

content.q: What happened to the KPI?
content.why: Đoạn 1: KPI **fell from 32% to 27%** trong hai quý.

content.why: Đoạn 2: kiểm tra số quan sát có giá trị bị thiếu.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Why is cleaning data so important?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Data scientists often say that they spend about eighty percent of their time on data cleaning. Raw data is rarely perfect. It can come from surveys, sensors, web scraping or company databases, and each source has its own format and problems.

Imagine a retail dataset. First, the team ingests the files into one system. Then they look for duplicates, for example two rows for the same order. Missing values are another problem: when customers skip a question, the age column stays empty. The team can remove those rows or impute the missing values with the median. Outliers must also be checked, because a price of ten million dollars is probably a typing error, but it could also be a real luxury sale.

Finally, the data is validated. If the quality is poor, every model will give poor results. This idea is often summed up as "garbage in, garbage out".

content.q: Data scientists often spend most of their time on data cleaning.
content.why: Đoạn 1: khoảng **80%** thời gian dành cho làm sạch dữ liệu.

content.q: Every data source uses exactly the same format.
content.why: Đoạn 1: mỗi nguồn có **format** và vấn đề riêng.

content.q: A price of ten million dollars is always a typing error.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'probably' một lỗi gõ, nhưng **cũng có thể** là giao dịch thật.

content.q: Poor-quality data usually leads to poor model results.
content.why: Đoạn 3: nếu chất lượng kém, mọi mô hình sẽ cho kết quả kém.

content.q: What can a team do with missing values?
content.why: Đoạn 2: xóa các dòng đó hoặc **impute** bằng trung vị.
opts: Remove the rows or impute them

content.q: Which problem is an example of a duplicate?
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'two rows for the same order'.
opts: Two rows for the same order

content.q: What does the team do first in the retail example?
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'First, the team ingests the files…'.
opts: It ingests the files into one system

content.q: What does "garbage in, garbage out" mean in the text?
content.why: Đoạn 3: dữ liệu kém → kết quả kém.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A hospital cleans its data
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A hospital in Da Nang wanted to predict which patients would return within thirty days. At first, the results were disappointing, so the data team studied the dataset more carefully.

They found three problems. First, the date of birth was written in four different formats, so the dates were parsed and converted to one standard format. Second, about twelve percent of the blood-pressure values were missing, because a sensor in one department was broken. These values were imputed using the average of similar patients. Third, many patients appeared twice, once with a full name and once with a short name, and the duplicates were merged using a patient ID.

After the cleaning, the team ran the model again. The accuracy rose from 68% to 81%. The head of the team said that clean data was more important than a complicated algorithm. The hospital has also introduced data validation rules, so that mistakes are caught when staff enter the information.

content.q: The first results of the model were disappointing.
content.why: Đoạn 1: 'the results were disappointing'.

content.q: The dates of birth were written in only one format.
content.why: Đoạn 2: ngày sinh có **four different formats**.

content.q: Duplicate patients were merged using a patient ID.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bản trùng được gộp bằng **patient ID**.

content.q: The accuracy fell after the cleaning.
content.why: Đoạn 3: độ chính xác **rose** từ 68% lên 81%.

content.q: Why were many blood-pressure values missing?
content.why: Đoạn 2: cảm biến ở một khoa bị hỏng.
opts: A sensor in one department was broken

content.q: How were the missing values imputed?
content.why: Đoạn 2: dùng giá trị trung bình của các bệnh nhân tương tự.
opts: Using the average of similar patients

content.q: What was the accuracy after cleaning?
content.why: Đoạn 3: accuracy tăng lên **81%**.

content.q: Why has the hospital introduced validation rules?
content.why: Đoạn 3: để phát hiện lỗi ngay khi nhân viên nhập liệu.
opts: To make the model more complicated
To catch mistakes when staff enter information

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Mean, median and the problem of outliers
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Imagine that five employees earn 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 million dong a month. The mean salary is 12 million, and the median is also 12 million. Now the company hires a director who earns 100 million. The mean rises to about 26.7 million, but the median increases only to 12.5 million. The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is not. That is why news reports often use the median income.

Spread is also important. Two classes can have the same mean score of 7.0, but in one class the standard deviation is 0.5 and in the other it is 2.0. In the second class, the scores are much more spread out. A histogram shows the distribution at a glance. If it has a long tail on one side, we say that it is skewed.

Finally, analysts must be careful with conclusions. A strong correlation between two variables does not prove causation. Another factor, a confounding variable, may explain both.

content.q: The mean salary was 12 million before the director joined.
content.why: Đoạn 1: trung bình ban đầu là **12 million**.

content.q: After the director joined, the median rose to 26.7 million.
content.why: Đoạn 1: **mean** tăng lên khoảng 26.7; median chỉ lên 12.5.

content.q: The median is more sensitive to outliers than the mean.
content.why: Đoạn 1: **mean** nhạy với outlier, median thì không.

content.q: A strong correlation proves that one variable causes the other.
content.why: Đoạn 3: tương quan mạnh **không** chứng minh nhân quả.

content.q: Why do news reports often use the median income?
content.why: Đoạn 1: mean nhạy cảm với giá trị ngoại lai.
opts: The mean is sensitive to outliers
The mean is hard to calculate

content.q: What is true about the two classes?
content.why: Đoạn 2: cùng mean 7.0, nhưng độ lệch chuẩn 0.5 và 2.0.
opts: They have the same standard deviation
They have the same mean but different standard deviations
The second class has a lower mean

content.q: What does a histogram show?
content.why: Đoạn 2: histogram cho thấy phân phối trong nháy mắt.

content.q: What could a confounding variable do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: biến gây nhiễu có thể giải thích cho cả hai biến.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Did the new button work?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Last month, an online shop ran an A/B test on its checkout page. Half of the visitors saw the old green button (version A), and the other half saw a new orange button (version B). Each group had about 20,000 visitors.

In version A, 4.0% of visitors completed a purchase. In version B, the figure rose to 4.4%, an increase of 0.4 percentage points. The analyst calculated a p-value of 0.03, which is lower than the usual threshold of 0.05, so the difference is statistically significant. The 95% confidence interval for the improvement was between 0.1 and 0.7 percentage points.

However, the analyst was careful with her wording. The result suggests that the orange button may increase sales, but the effect appears to be small. The test ran only during a holiday week, so customers might behave differently in other months. She recommended a second test before the company changes the design for all users.

content.q: Each version was shown to about 20,000 visitors.
content.why: Đoạn 1: mỗi nhóm có khoảng **20,000** khách.

content.q: Version B had a lower purchase rate than version A.
content.why: Đoạn 2: tỷ lệ mua của B **rose** lên 4.4%.

content.q: The p-value was higher than 0.05.
content.why: Đoạn 2: p-value là **0.03**, thấp hơn 0.05.

content.q: The test was run during a holiday week.
content.why: Đoạn 3: 'The test ran only during a holiday week'.

content.q: How much did the purchase rate increase?
content.why: Đoạn 2: tăng từ 4.0% lên 4.4% = **0.4 điểm phần trăm**.

content.q: What does the confidence interval show?
content.why: Đoạn 2: khoảng tin cậy 95% của mức cải thiện là 0.1–0.7 điểm.
opts: The improvement is probably between 0.1 and 0.7 points

content.q: Why was the analyst careful with her wording?
content.why: Đoạn 3: bài test chỉ chạy tuần lễ và hiệu ứng có vẻ nhỏ.
opts: The test ran only in a holiday week and the effect is small
The button colours were the same

content.q: What did she recommend?
content.why: Đoạn 3: cô đề xuất **a second test**.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Choosing the right chart
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Choosing the right chart is the first step of good data visualization. Every chart answers a different question. If you want to compare categories, a bar chart is usually the best choice, because the length of each bar is easy to compare. A line chart shows how a value changes over time, so it is ideal for a time series such as daily website visits. A scatter plot shows the relationship between two numerical variables, and a histogram shows how values are distributed. A pie chart can show parts of a whole, but it becomes difficult to read when there are more than five slices.

Colour also matters. A heatmap uses a colour scale to show high and low values in a grid, and a darker colour normally means a higher value. However, designers should avoid using too many colours, because clutter makes it harder for the audience to find the message.

Finally, always add a clear title, labels on both axes and a legend if needed.

content.q: A bar chart is a good way to compare categories.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bar chart thường là lựa chọn tốt nhất để so sánh các nhóm.

content.q: A pie chart is easy to read with many slices.
content.why: Đoạn 1: pie chart khó đọc khi có **hơn năm** phần.

content.q: A scatter plot shows the relationship between two numerical variables.
content.why: Đoạn 1: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: A heatmap normally uses darker colours for lower values.
content.why: Đoạn 2: màu đậm hơn thường nghĩa là giá trị **cao hơn**.

content.q: Which chart is ideal for a time series?
content.why: Đoạn 1: line chart lý tưởng cho chuỗi thời gian.

content.q: Why can too many colours be a problem?
content.why: Đoạn 2: gây rối mắt, khó tìm thông điệp.

content.q: What does a histogram show?
content.why: Đoạn 1: histogram cho thấy cách các giá trị phân bố.

content.q: What should always be added to a chart?
content.why: Đoạn 3: tiêu đề rõ ràng, nhãn cho cả hai trục.
opts: A clear title and labels on both axes

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A misleading chart
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Last year, a company showed a bar chart in its annual report. The chart compared the profit of two years: $98 million and $102 million. Because the y-axis started at 97 instead of 0, the second bar looked five times taller than the first one. As a result, many readers believed that profit had increased dramatically.

A journalist noticed the problem and published a corrected version. In the new chart, the axis started at zero, and the difference between the bars was small. The journalist also added an annotation that said, "Profit increased by about 4%." Due to the criticism, the company apologised and changed its design rules.

The story teaches three lessons. First, a scale that does not start at zero can mislead the audience. Second, a good visualization should help people understand the data, not influence their opinion. Third, a clear caption and annotations lead to better decisions.

content.q: The profits in the two years were $98 million and $102 million.
content.why: Đoạn 1: lợi nhuận hai năm là 98 và 102 triệu đô.

content.q: The y-axis started at zero in the original chart.
content.why: Đoạn 1: trục y bắt đầu từ **97**, không phải 0.

content.q: The journalist published a corrected chart.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nhà báo đăng bản biểu đồ đã sửa.

content.q: The company ignored the criticism.
content.why: Đoạn 2: công ty **xin lỗi** và đổi quy tắc thiết kế.

content.q: Why did the second bar look so tall?
content.why: Đoạn 1: do trục y bắt đầu từ 97.
opts: The profit was five times higher

content.q: What did the journalist add?
content.why: Đoạn 2: ghi chú 'Profit increased by about 4%'.

content.q: What was the result of the criticism?
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'Due to the criticism, the company apologised…'.
opts: The company apologised and changed its design rules

content.q: What is one lesson of the story?
content.why: Đoạn 3: bài học đầu tiên về thang đo không bắt đầu từ 0.
opts: A scale that does not start at zero can mislead people

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How a model learns
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Machine learning is a way of building software that learns from data instead of following fixed rules. Imagine that a bank wants to find fraud. The team collects thousands of past transactions, and each one has a label: fraud or not fraud. This is supervised learning, because the model learns from examples with known answers. The team splits the data into training data and test data.

During training, the algorithm adjusts its parameters to reduce a loss function, which measures how wrong the predictions are. A method called gradient descent makes small changes step by step, and each full pass through the data is an epoch. If the model learns the training data too well, it memorises noise, and this is called overfitting. An overfitted model performs very well on the training data but badly on new transactions.

To check this, the team evaluates the model on the test data, which it has never seen. If the results are good, the model can be used for inference on live transactions.

content.q: In supervised learning, the examples have known labels.
content.why: Đoạn 1: học có giám sát dùng ví dụ **có đáp án**.

content.q: A loss function measures how wrong the predictions are.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: An overfitted model performs badly on the training data.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nó chạy **rất tốt** trên training data nhưng tệ trên dữ liệu mới.

content.q: The model is evaluated on the training data only.
content.why: Đoạn 3: mô hình được đánh giá trên **test data**.

content.q: What does the bank want to find?

content.why: Đoạn 2: 'each full pass through the data is an epoch'.
opts: One full pass through the training data

content.why: Đoạn 2: thay đổi nhỏ từng bước để giảm loss.
opts: It makes small changes step by step to reduce the loss

content.q: Why does the team use test data?
content.why: Đoạn 3: để kiểm tra trên dữ liệu mô hình chưa từng thấy.
opts: To check how the model performs on data it has never seen

exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Many beginners ask which algorithm they should choose. The honest answer is that it depends on the problem and the data.

A linear regression is a simple model that is easy to explain. It works well when the relationship between the features and the target is close to a straight line. A decision tree is a model that asks a series of questions, so it is easy to visualise, but a single tree often overfits. A random forest, which combines many trees, is usually more accurate and more stable. Deep neural networks are powerful when you have a huge amount of data, for example millions of images, but they need more computing power and are harder to interpret.

Experienced data scientists always start with a baseline. If a simple model already gives acceptable results, a complex model may not be worth the extra cost. Unless the improvement is clear, they keep the simpler solution.

content.q: The best algorithm is always a neural network.
content.why: Đoạn 1: câu trả lời là **tùy bài toán và dữ liệu**.

content.q: A single decision tree often overfits.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'a single tree often overfits'.

content.q: A random forest combines many trees.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: Experienced data scientists start with a complex model.
content.why: Đoạn 3: họ bắt đầu bằng một **baseline** đơn giản.

content.q: When does linear regression work well?
content.why: Đoạn 2: khi quan hệ gần với đường thẳng.
opts: When the relationship is close to a straight line
When there are millions of images

content.q: Why are deep neural networks harder to use?
content.why: Đoạn 2: cần nhiều sức tính toán và khó diễn giải hơn.
opts: They need more computing power and are harder to interpret

content.q: What do experienced data scientists do first?

content.why: Đoạn 3: 'Unless the improvement is clear, they keep the simpler solution.'
opts: Unless the improvement from a complex model is clear

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Accuracy is not enough
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A hospital built a model to detect a rare disease that affects only 1% of patients. The model predicted "healthy" for every patient, and its accuracy was 99%. The team was happy at first, but then a doctor asked how many sick patients the model had found. The answer was zero.

This example shows why accuracy can be misleading with imbalanced data. A confusion matrix is more useful, because it shows true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives. From these numbers, data scientists calculate precision and recall. Precision tells us how many of the patients that the model marked as sick were really sick. Recall tells us how many of the sick patients the model found. In medicine, a false negative is dangerous, so recall is often the priority.

The F1 score combines precision and recall in one number. The team also changed the threshold, which lowered the cut-off for predicting "sick". As a result, recall rose from 0% to 78%, although precision fell.

content.q: The disease affects 1% of patients.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bệnh chỉ ảnh hưởng **1%** bệnh nhân.

content.q: The first model found many sick patients.
content.why: Đoạn 1: số bệnh nhân mô hình tìm được là **zero**.

content.q: Recall tells us how many of the sick patients the model found.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: After the threshold changed, recall fell.
content.why: Đoạn 3: recall **rose** từ 0% lên 78%.

content.q: Why was 99% accuracy misleading?
content.why: Đoạn 1: mô hình đoán 'healthy' cho tất cả, mà 99% bệnh nhân khỏe.
opts: The model predicted healthy for everyone
The model had a high recall

content.q: Why is recall often the priority in medicine?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bỏ sót ca bệnh (false negative) rất nguy hiểm.

content.q: What does a confusion matrix show?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nó hiển thị TP, FP, TN, FN.
opts: True and false positives and negatives

content.q: What happened when the team lowered the cut-off?
content.why: Đoạn 3: recall tăng lên 78% còn precision giảm.
opts: Recall rose to 78%, but precision fell

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Why models fail in production
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A model is not finished when training ends. Many projects fail after deployment. One company built a model that predicted delivery times, and it worked well for six months. Then customer behaviour changed, new cities were added and the model's error increased. This is called model drift.

To avoid this problem, teams use MLOps. First, every trained model is saved in a model registry with its version, its data and its metrics. Next, an automated pipeline deploys the model to a live system. Monitoring tools track latency, errors and the quality of predictions, and they send an alert when the performance falls. If the accuracy drops below a threshold, the team retrains the model with fresh data.

Teams also have to choose between batch prediction, which runs once a day on many records, and real-time prediction, which answers each request in milliseconds. Real-time systems are more expensive, so a team should use them only when the business really needs them.

content.q: The delivery-time model failed immediately after deployment.
content.why: Đoạn 1: nó chạy tốt trong **sáu tháng**.

content.q: A model registry stores the version, the data and the metrics of a model.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: Monitoring tools send an alert when performance falls.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'they send an alert when the performance falls'.

content.q: Real-time systems are cheaper than batch systems.
content.why: Đoạn 3: real-time **đắt hơn**.

content.q: What is model drift?
content.why: Đoạn 1: hành vi khách hàng thay đổi nên lỗi mô hình tăng.
opts: The model's error increases because the real world changes

content.q: What does the team do if accuracy drops below the threshold?
content.why: Đoạn 2: huấn luyện lại với dữ liệu mới.
opts: It retrains the model with fresh data

content.q: What is batch prediction?
content.why: Đoạn 3: chạy mỗi ngày một lần trên nhiều bản ghi.
opts: Predictions that run once a day on many records

content.q: When should a team use real-time prediction?
content.why: Đoạn 3: chỉ dùng khi doanh nghiệp thật sự cần.
opts: Only when the business really needs it

exercises.title: Bài 1 · The Vs of big data
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Big data does not simply mean a large file. Experts often describe it with the three Vs: volume, velocity and variety. Volume is the amount of data; a social network may store petabytes of photos. Velocity is the speed at which new data arrives, for example thousands of payments per second. Variety describes the different formats: tables, text, images and sensor data. Some experts add a fourth V, veracity, which means how reliable the data is.

A single computer cannot process this amount of data, so engineers use a distributed system. A cluster consists of many machines, called nodes, which work in parallel. Hadoop was one of the first open-source frameworks for this task. Its file system, HDFS, splits large files into blocks and keeps copies on several nodes, so the system is fault-tolerant: if one node fails, the data is still safe.

Today, many companies prefer cloud storage because it is scalable. They can add more nodes when the volume grows and remove them when it falls.

content.q: Big data simply means a large file.
content.why: Đoạn 1: big data không chỉ là một tệp lớn mà còn gồm **volume, velocity, variety**.

content.q: Velocity describes how fast new data arrives.
content.why: Đoạn 1: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: In HDFS, copies of the data are kept on several nodes.
content.why: Đoạn 2: HDFS giữ bản sao trên nhiều node.

content.q: A single computer can process any amount of data.
content.why: Đoạn 2: một máy **không thể** xử lý lượng dữ liệu này.

content.q: What does variety describe?
content.why: Đoạn 1: variety = các định dạng khác nhau.

content.q: What does veracity mean?
content.why: Đoạn 1: veracity = độ tin cậy của dữ liệu.

content.q: Why is HDFS fault-tolerant?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nếu một node hỏng, dữ liệu vẫn an toàn nhờ bản sao.
opts: It keeps copies of data on several nodes

content.q: Why do many companies prefer cloud storage?
content.why: Đoạn 3: vì nó có thể mở rộng thêm hoặc bớt node.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Batch or streaming?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A ride-hailing company collects data from millions of trips. Its engineers have two different needs. In the morning, managers want a report about yesterday's trips. This job is done by batch processing: every night, a Spark job reads the raw files from the data lake, cleans them and loads the results into a data warehouse. The job takes two hours, and nobody minds, because the report is only needed at 8 a.m.

The second need is more urgent. If a driver's app sends strange GPS data, the system must raise an alert within seconds. For this, the company uses stream processing. Each event is sent to a message queue, and a streaming job reads it immediately. The data is divided into partitions, so that many workers can process it in parallel.

The architecture is more complex than a single database, but it is based on a simple idea: use the right tool for each task. An orchestration tool schedules the batch jobs, and a data catalog helps analysts to find the tables they need.

content.q: The nightly report is produced by batch processing.
content.why: Đoạn 1: job chạy mỗi đêm là **batch processing**.

content.q: The batch job takes two minutes.
content.why: Đoạn 1: job mất **two hours**.

content.q: Streaming jobs read events immediately from a message queue.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'a streaming job reads it immediately'.

content.q: A data catalog schedules the batch jobs.
content.why: Đoạn 3: **orchestration tool** lên lịch job; data catalog giúp tìm bảng dữ liệu.

content.q: Where does the batch job read the raw files from?
content.why: Đoạn 1: đọc file thô từ **data lake**.

content.q: Why is stream processing used for GPS alerts?
content.why: Đoạn 2: hệ thống phải báo động trong vài giây.
opts: The system must react within seconds
The report is needed at 8 a.m.

content.q: Why is the data divided into partitions?
content.why: Đoạn 2: để nhiều worker xử lý song song.
opts: So that many workers can process it in parallel
So it fits in a spreadsheet

content.q: What is the simple idea behind the architecture?
content.why: Đoạn 3: dùng đúng công cụ cho từng việc.
opts: Use the right tool for each task

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Data and privacy
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Every time we use an app, we leave data behind: our location, our searches and our purchases. Companies can use this personal data to improve services, but they must also protect people's privacy. In Europe, the GDPR says that organisations must get clear consent before they collect personal data. Users are allowed to see their data, to correct it and to ask the company to delete it. A company that breaks the rules may have to pay a heavy penalty.

Data teams use several methods to protect privacy. Anonymization removes names and other details so that nobody can identify a person. Pseudonymization replaces the identifiers with codes, but the data is still personal, because someone who has the key can reverse the process. Sensitive attributes, such as health or religion, need extra protection, and access control makes sure that only authorised staff can open the files.

Privacy also depends on retention. A retention policy tells a company how long it may keep data. When the period ends, the data must be deleted. An audit trail records who accessed the data, which helps the company prove compliance.

content.q: Under the GDPR, companies must get consent before collecting personal data.
content.why: Đoạn 1: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: Users are not allowed to ask a company to delete their data.
content.why: Đoạn 1: người dùng **được phép** yêu cầu xóa dữ liệu.

content.q: Pseudonymized data is no longer personal data.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nó **vẫn là dữ liệu cá nhân**, vì ai có khóa có thể đảo ngược.

content.q: An audit trail records who accessed the data.
content.why: Đoạn 3: đúng nguyên văn.

content.q: What may happen to a company that breaks the rules?
content.why: Đoạn 1: có thể bị phạt nặng.
opts: It may have to pay a heavy penalty

content.q: What does anonymization do?
content.why: Đoạn 2: xóa tên và chi tiết để không ai nhận ra người đó.
opts: It replaces identifiers with a key
It removes details so that nobody can identify a person
It records who accessed the data

content.q: What does a retention policy tell a company?
content.why: Đoạn 3: được giữ dữ liệu bao lâu.
opts: How long it may keep data

content.q: Which data needs extra protection?
content.why: Đoạn 2: thuộc tính nhạy cảm như sức khỏe, tôn giáo.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A data science job interview
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Last week, Minh had an interview for a junior data scientist position. The interviewer, Ms Hanh, started by asking him whether he had any experience with real projects. Minh said that he had completed an internship at a logistics company, where he had built a model to predict delivery times. He added that he was keeping all his work in an online portfolio.

Then Ms Hanh asked what he would do if his model had very high accuracy on the training data but poor results on the test data. Minh answered that he would suspect overfitting. He explained that he would simplify the model, add more data and use cross-validation. She also asked how he explained results to people who did not know statistics. He said that he used simple charts and short stories instead of formulas.

At the end, Ms Hanh told him that the team valued communication as much as technical skills. She said that the company would contact him within a week. Minh felt that the interview had gone well, and he was already preparing for the next one by learning Spark.

content.q: Minh did an internship at a logistics company.
content.why: Đoạn 1: anh ấy thực tập tại một công ty logistics.

content.q: Minh kept his work in an online portfolio.
content.why: Đoạn 1: 'all his work in an online portfolio'.

content.q: Ms Hanh said that the team valued only technical skills.
content.why: Đoạn 3: đội coi trọng **giao tiếp** bằng kỹ năng kỹ thuật.

content.q: Minh would ignore the problem if the test results were poor.
content.why: Đoạn 2: anh ấy nghi ngờ **overfitting** và sẽ đơn giản hóa mô hình, thêm dữ liệu, dùng cross-validation.

content.q: What did Minh build during his internship?
content.why: Đoạn 1: mô hình dự đoán thời gian giao hàng.
opts: A model to predict delivery times

content.q: What would Minh suspect if training accuracy was high but test results were poor?
content.why: Đoạn 2: anh ấy trả lời sẽ nghi ngờ **overfitting**.

content.q: How did Minh explain results to people who did not know statistics?
content.why: Đoạn 2: dùng biểu đồ đơn giản và câu chuyện ngắn.
opts: With simple charts and short stories

content.q: When would the company contact him?
content.why: Đoạn 3: công ty sẽ liên hệ trong vòng một tuần.
